consensus_summary: Grass primarily symbolizes the transience, frailty, and mortality of human life/flesh (brief flourishing then withering), anchored in Isa 40:6-8 and parallels; secondary uses include divine provision, short-lived wicked prosperity, or abundance.
book_summary: Grass means mortal people or flesh growing across the field until they wither or are gathered at harvest.
consensus_core_identification: transience/mortality of human life or flesh (people likened to withering grass)
book_core_identification: mortal people or flesh (growing in the field to wither or harvest)
boundary_disagreement: Book adds growth across the field plus gathering at harvest as terminal outcomes, extending beyond the consensus focus on withering/transience alone.
rationale: Both cores identify the same referent (mortal people/flesh via the Isa 40 equation). The book preserves that category but materially widens extension and conditions by incorporating field-growth and harvest-gathering (via the Matt 13:38 cross-reference), which consensus does not treat as standard for grass.
strongest_objection: Matt 13:38 concerns seed/tares in the field, not grass; harvest-gathering is grain imagery, so the book's added terminus may not properly attach to grass.
